liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Terrapin Station** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer loved this Terrapin as heard on the King Biscuit Flower Hour broadcast; The King Biscuit broadcast version of Terrapin is called one of the best the reviewer has heard [1][12][13][22]
- **Jack Straw** (3 reviews): Reviewer found the opening Jack Straw tremendous, a high-energy start; The band came out burning with Jack Straw, which the reviewer relistened to on Go To Nassau [15][21][23]
- **Peggy-O** (2 reviews): Peggy-O is named among the show's strong points, alongside Jack Straw; Reviewer remembers a beautiful Peggy-O [19][21]
- **Cassidy** (1 other source): The end of Cassidy, from 4:20 onward, is supplied from shnid 34721 [5]
- **// Althea** (1 review): Althea is called stupendously weak, far less muscular than it should have been [19]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): The Playin' into Uncle John's Band segment is singled out as memorable [13]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Uncle John's comes together; Billy and Mickey gather everyone in the last minutes while Jerry snarls the close [14]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Good Lovin' was also part of the radio broadcast and has always ranked high for the reviewer [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-15.aud.long.34721.sbeok.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 158 min [1]. Said about its sound: IZotope Ozone adjusted the sound of the FM patches to blend with the audience source [1]
- **gd1980-05-15.150726.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac24**: source not stated; 24 songs; 159 min [2]
- **gd1980-05-15.126692.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 159 min; rated 4.78/5 by 9 [4]
- **gd1980-05-15.sbd.cantor.miller.93426.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 152 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [5]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds nice overall, though with some rough patches [17]
- **gd80-05-15.aud.schlissel.12790.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 158 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first live Dead show after nine years of listening; it settled their devotion to the band [15]
- Reviewer sat in the very first row, tickets arranged by a friend named Peter [21]
- Reviewer first heard this show on the radio in 1980 [22]
- Brent's voice sounds high here and clashes with Jerry's; it later deepened and became more bluesy [17]
- Spring/Summer 1980 is an overlooked era; the reviewer prefers audience tapes from it over soundboards, which catch Brent's toy piano and organ noises [19]
- Less wandering than earlier shows, but for 1980s New York Dead it's hard to beat, perhaps besides 1983 MSG shows [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-15.aud.long.34721.sbeok.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Andrew Long; source: AUD MC > DAT > CDR > EAC > Cool Edit 2K > CDWave > SHN [1]. Also: Audience source (Schlissel, shnid 12790) patched with FM broadcast material from shnid 34685, taken via cassette on a Sony TC-D5M [1]
- **gd1980-05-15.150726.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac24**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: FOB Nakamichi CM700 > Cassette Master (Maxell UDXLII) [2]. Also: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad mastered by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller, with pitch correction; Shnid 126082 supplies patches for Uncle John's Band [2]
- **gd1980-05-15.126692.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 Source Matrix by dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:93426) Recording Info: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat (48k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony R500) -> VXPocket v2 ->… [4]. Also: This is a matrix recording credited to Dusborne, with show information embedded in the flac file headers [4]
- **gd1980-05-15.sbd.cantor.miller.93426.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master [5]. Also: Taken from Betty's recording mix, with DATs lent by Rob Eaton; numerous mix changes occur throughout the show; Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad comes from unknown mics, cassette master, DAT, then CD (shnid 34721) [5]
- **gd80-05-15.aud.schlissel.12790.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [6]. Also: Reviewer first knew this show from a King Biscuit Flower Hour tape [14]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum - May 15, 1980](https://www.dead.net/show/may-15-1980) [25]
